organizerGuidelines.intro: Rules for hosting events on spotto, plus our policies on sales, payouts, and troubleshooting. Please review them separately from the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy for attendees.

rules.title: 1. Event hosting rules
paragraphs: To help attendees sign up with confidence, organizers must set and publish accurate dates, locations, fees, and cancellation terms.
Events with false information, events that violate laws or public order and morals, and events that infringe on the rights of third parties may not be listed. We may remove or unpublish such events.
bullets: Make sure the listing matches what actually takes place
If minors will participate, take appropriate steps such as obtaining parental consent
Organizers are responsible for arranging venues and equipment and for safety management
Do not engage in harassment or discriminatory behavior in chat or in person

fees.title: 2. How fees work (platform fee)
paragraphs: Payments for paid events incur payment processing fees and the spotto platform fee (a flat 10%).
The organizer’s payable amount (sales) is the total paid by attendees minus the platform fee (10%) and payment processing fees.

payout.title: 3. Receiving sales and payouts
paragraphs: spotto holds the ticket payments made by attendees and later pays them out to the organizer.
bullets: Before your first payout, register bank account details in your own name on the “Bank account” screen

[Important] Always register the account under your own legal name. If an account in someone else’s name or false information is registered, we may suspend payouts, freeze the account, or forfeit sales without prior notice

Payout schedule: closed at the end of each month and paid at the end of the following month (sales from events held and completed during the month are paid together to your registered account at the end of the next month)
A flat transfer fee of ¥500 (tax included) is deducted from each payout. Please also watch out for payout delays caused by errors in your account information

cancel.title: 4. Cancellation and refund policy
paragraphs: Always set and state each event’s cancellation policy (for example, until when a full refund is available and whether refunds are unavailable afterward) when creating the event.
If a cancellation or refund occurs after purchase, we will handle it appropriately based on the configured cancellation policy and the payment result (or process it via the Stripe dashboard).

trouble.title: 5. Prohibited acts and handling of disputes
paragraphs: If an organizer or attendee cancels on the day of an event, or a dispute over money or personal relationships arises between participants, please make a good-faith effort to resolve it between yourselves.

If we find that an account in someone else’s name has been registered, false information has been entered, or other malicious violations have occurred, we may, at our discretion, take strict measures such as suspending the account or forfeiting sales.
